qa_pairs.instruction: What is the role of the Name Service Switch in account redirection for the Fan-Out driver?
qa_pairs.output: In the Fan-Out driver, the Name Service Switch (NSS) redirects requests for account information—such as uidNumber, gidNumber, or homeDirectory—to the library that is specified in the NSS configuration file. This enables the Fan-Out driver to obtain account data from the appropriate source.

qa_pairs.instruction: Which configuration file does the Fan-Out driver rely on for Name Service Switch library selection?
What types of account information can be redirected through the Name Service Switch when using the Fan-Out driver?
qa_pairs.output: When using the Fan-Out driver, the Name Service Switch can redirect requests for uidNumber, gidNumber, and homeDirectory.

qa_pairs.instruction: When the Fan-Out driver is configured to use the Platform Services Cache Daemon, from where is the account information retrieved?
qa_pairs.output: If the Fan-Out driver is configured to use the Platform Services Cache Daemon, account information is retrieved from the Event Journal Services memory cache that resides on the local Linux or UNIX system.

qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize how the Name Service Switch and Platform Services Cache Daemon work together with the Fan-Out driver to provide account information.
qa_pairs.output: The Fan-Out driver can use the Name Service Switch (configured via /etc/nsswitch.conf) to redirect account queries such as uidNumber, gidNumber, or homeDirectory. When the Platform Services Cache Daemon is enabled, those queries are satisfied from the Event Journal Services memory cache on the local host, providing fast local access to account data.
